name: Disable 'Enhance pointer precision' (mouse acceleration)
description: Makes desktop cursor movement proportional to physical mouse movement.
mechanism: Sets MouseSpeed, MouseThreshold1 and MouseThreshold2 to "0" under HKCU\Control Panel\Mouse and applies them to the running session with SystemParametersInfo(SPI_SETMOUSE).
benefit: Consistent aim/muscle memory in games that use the Windows cursor (many menus, RTS/MOBA games, some older shooters).
drawback: The cursor may feel slower at low speeds; adjust pointer speed or mouse DPI. Games using raw input are unaffected either way.
evidence: Standard Mouse Properties setting. It does not change input latency — only the acceleration curve.

name: Disable the Sticky Keys shortcut (Shift ×5)
description: Stops pressing Shift five times from opening the Sticky Keys prompt mid-game.
mechanism: Clears only the hotkey bit (0x4) of HKCU\Control Panel\Accessibility\StickyKeys\Flags. Other bits are preserved, so Sticky Keys stays on if you actively use it.
benefit: Prevents the game from being minimised by the accessibility prompt.
drawback: The keyboard shortcut no longer toggles Sticky Keys; use Settings › Accessibility › Keyboard instead.
recommendedFor: All gamers who don't use the shortcut.
evidence: Flag bits documented for STICKYKEYS (SKF_HOTKEYACTIVE = 0x4). Read at sign-in.

name: Disable the Toggle Keys shortcut (hold Num Lock 5 s)
description: Stops holding Num Lock from turning on Toggle Keys.
mechanism: Clears the hotkey bit (0x4) of HKCU\Control Panel\Accessibility\ToggleKeys\Flags, preserving other bits.
benefit: Avoids an accessibility prompt interrupting games.
drawback: The shortcut no longer works; Toggle Keys remains available in Settings.
recommendedFor: Gamers who don't use the shortcut.

name: Disable the Filter Keys shortcut (hold right Shift 8 s)
description: Stops holding right Shift from turning on Filter Keys, which ignores brief keystrokes.
mechanism: Clears the hotkey bit (0x4) of HKCU\Control Panel\Accessibility\Keyboard Response\Flags, preserving other bits.
benefit: Prevents accidentally enabling Filter Keys, which makes key presses appear to be ignored in games.
drawback: The shortcut no longer works; Filter Keys remains available in Settings.
recommendedFor: Gamers who don't use the shortcut.

name: Fastest keyboard repeat delay and rate
description: Sets the shortest repeat delay and the fastest repeat rate for held keys.
mechanism: Sets KeyboardDelay="0" (≈250 ms) and KeyboardSpeed="31" (≈30 repeats/s) under HKCU\Control Panel\Keyboard — the extremes of the Keyboard Properties sliders.
benefit: Held keys repeat sooner in text fields and games that rely on OS key repeat.
drawback: Personal preference; may cause accidental repeated characters when typing. Games using raw/DirectInput are unaffected.
recommendedFor: Users who prefer fast key repeat.
evidence: Documented Control Panel values. Not an input-latency change.
